name: Agentic Report Authoring (Plan → Design → Author → Validate → Publish)
description: Author a Power BI report end-to-end from natural language with fabio — the same Plan → Design → Author → Validate → Publish pipeline as Microsoft's first-party Power BI Report Authoring agent skill (Skills for Fabric, June 2026), but HEADLESS and CI-friendly: fabio edits the PBIR definition over REST and publishes straight to a Fabric workspace (no Power BI Desktop / Desktop Bridge, no local PBIP required).
prerequisites: Authenticated via fabio auth login (or az login)
A published semantic model to bind the report to (the 'dataset'); get its id from fabio semantic-model list
Familiarity with the PBIR report definition (fabio context schema Report)

steps.command: fabio semantic-model list --workspace $WS_ID && fabio semantic-model list-tables --workspace $WS_ID --id $SM_ID && fabio semantic-model list-measures --workspace $WS_ID --id $SM_ID
steps.description: PLAN. Establish the data foundation and requirements: pick the semantic model (dataset) the report will bind to, and inspect its tables/columns/measures so every visual references REAL fields (Table.Column, or an aggregation like Sum(Table.Column)). For an EXISTING report you are revising, use `report copilot-metadata --id $REPORT_ID` to read its synthesized schema (pages, visuals, field bindings).

DESIGN. Choose page archetypes (overview, detail, KPI), a visual per insight, and a layout. Valid visual types come from `report add-visual --type` (card, clusteredBarChart, clusteredColumnChart, lineChart, pieChart, tableEx, slicer, textbox, …). Ground the design in the PBIR schema so pages/visuals conform to their published $schema.

AUTHOR. Generate the whole report from one compact JSON spec: {"pages":[{"displayName":"Overview","visuals":[{"type":"card","measure":"Sum(Sales.Amount)"},{"type":"clusteredColumnChart","category":"Product.Category","measure":"Sum(Sales.Amount)"}]}]}. Fields use Table.Column DOT form (Sales.Amount, NOT Sales[Amount]); measures wrap an aggregation like Sum(Sales.Amount). --out writes the PBIR folder to disk (for source control / validation) INSTEAD of creating it; omit --out to create directly. For incremental edits use add-page / add-visual / rename-page / set-active-page / delete-visual (a definition read-modify-write).

VALIDATE. Validate the PBIR (or PBIR-Legacy) definition on disk BEFORE publishing — it checks the definition against the PBIR schema and catches structural errors early. For an already-created report, `report list-pages` / `list-visuals` confirm the pages and data bindings landed as intended.

PUBLISH. Push the validated PBIR folder to the Fabric workspace bound to the semantic model. (If you scaffolded WITHOUT --out in step 3, the report is already created — skip this.) Optionally `report export --format pdf|pptx|png` to render it, or `report publish-to-web` for a public embed URL. Promote across environments with `fabio deploy apply` (see workflow cicd-deploy).

notes: This is fabio's answer to Microsoft's Power BI Report Authoring agent skill (Skills for Fabric): the SAME five stages, but fabio is headless (REST, no Desktop Bridge), operates on the deployed workspace item OR a local PBIR folder, and slots into CI/CD via deploy. See 'fabio context best-practices agentic-reporting'. For the report-CONSUMPTION side (chat-with-your-data, the Fabric IQ analog), publish a data agent (fabio data-agent publish -> MCP/consumption URL) or query an ontology graph. PBIR is Microsoft's documented, agent-authorable format and becomes the ONLY report format at GA — always `report validate` before create/deploy.
